nodes.name: Page Loop
nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 1 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.name: Split Result Items
nodes.notes: Explodes the data array into one item per element.

nodes.name: Normalize Page Items
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming listing records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Remove Duplicate Listings
nodes.notes: Drops duplicates within this run (compared on listingId). Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Upsert Harvest into Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Listing Tracker', matched on listingId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Tally Harvest Stats
nodes.notes: Group-by + aggregate (like a pivot table) — turns raw rows into KPI numbers.

# Extract listings with PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** Web Scraping · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers listings work end to end across PostgreSQL, Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 30 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Init Cursor
3. Page Loop
4. Fetch Page from API
5. Split Result Items
6. Normalize Page Items
7. Remove Duplicate Listings
8. Upsert Harvest into Google Sheets
9. Tally Harvest Stats
10. Load Previous Snapshot
11. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
12. Enrich with Reference Data
13. Fold In Enrichment Fields
14. Stamp Completion Time
15. Persist Run Metadata
16. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
17. Record Sub-workflow Result
18. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
19. Archive Row Snapshot
20. Fingerprint for Idempotency
21. Drop Already-Processed Items
22. Cap Batch Volume
23. Align Field Names
24. Tag Pipeline Metadata
25. Save Execution Metadata
26. Stamp Processing Time
27. Guard Non-Empty url
28. Summarize Run Stats
29. Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL)
30. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing listings work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Init Cursor → Page Loop → Fetch Page from API → Split Result Items → Normalize Page Items → Remove Duplicate Listings → Upsert Harvest into Google Sheets → Tally Harvest Stats → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty url → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and Slack aligned by hand for listings
- A backlog too large to push into PostgreSQL in one pass, across 33 nodes
- Listings work where "Init Cursor" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Listings work that only reaches PostgreSQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and Slack in step for listings, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in PostgreSQL or Slack are skipped, across all 33 nodes of this listings build
- A failed PostgreSQL or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 33 nodes in this listings build
- Batches the work so PostgreSQL rate limits never break a listings run
- Every listings run leaves an audit row behind, alongside PostgreSQL

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Split In Batches drives the pagination loop instead of a fixed number of HTTP calls, because the page count isn't known upfront — the loop output feeds back into itself until the source stops returning data. Fetching one page per iteration, not all pages at once, keeps memory bounded even against a source with tens of thousands of records.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Change the page-size parameter and watch how many loop iterations it takes to finish.
2. Add a hard cap (a Limit node) so a runaway source can't loop forever.
3. Point the fetch target at a real paginated API and adjust the cursor logic to match its response shape.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your listings process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole listings payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
